_doc: Each entry: { file: relative path from repo root, lines: [int,...] | "*" for whole file, reason: short justification }. Use sparingly — first ask whether the file should be neutralized or carved out. Policy cap: > 20 entries means the linter (or the content) is wrong — fix the tool or the text, never grow the list. Rebuilt 2026-07-12 (road-to-opt-hygiene-and-debt Phase 1): 104 → minimal set after heuristic upgrades + 25 content neutralizations + 2 carve-outs.

entries.reason: Worked PHP docblock demo inside the rule's own wrong/right example block — quoted teaching content.
Quoted example of a framework-internal behavior explicitly marked as what NOT to test — meta content, not a mandate.
Example learnings/decisions quoted verbatim in the promotion-flow walkthrough — meta content.
Tool-intrinsic install lines — markitdown IS a pip package; the install command is the tool's identity, not stack leakage.

Canonical multi-stack module catalogue (Laravel HMVC / Symfony DDD / Node / Python sections) — keep-in-place is a recorded council decision; per-stack sections sit farther apart than the ±10-line window.
Quoted example ticket title ('upgrade Laravel to 11') illustrating when discovery adds noise — meta content.
Tool-intrinsic install line — repomix IS an npm package.
Quoted rule-description example (the php-coding rule's own description string) — meta content.
Multi-ecosystem XSS row (Blade/JSX/Jinja peers on one line) + a quoted false-positive example ('Laravel's CSRF is already handled') — documentation, not a mandate.
Quoted anti-example ('❌ Describing how Laravel middleware works') — the line teaches what NOT to write.
Quoted description examples + the 'too-broad skill (Laravel skill)' anti-pattern — meta content.
Per-ecosystem check commands in fenced blocks; the pip/composer siblings sit farther apart than the ±10-line window — genuine multi-ecosystem documentation.
Worked Example A (PHP/Pest) paired with Example B (TypeScript/Jest) farther apart than the ±10-line window — canonical two-stack demo.
Multi-ecosystem capture-tools line and skip-marker grep spanning pytest/PHPUnit/JS in one pattern — documentation across stacks.

Example A of a deliberate A/B pair: '### Example A — PHP / Pest' (L228) sits opposite '### Example B — TypeScript / Vitest' (L259). That is framework-neutrality's textbook 'multi-stack peers' shape, but the two headings are 31 lines apart and the cross-stack window is +/-10, so the heuristic cannot see the sibling. Allowlisted rather than widening the window for a single document — if a second per-stack A/B skill appears, build the section-aware window instead of adding a second entry here.
